## Wang Yangming quote sources

9 passages attributed to Wang Yangming in this archive, each with the locator that lets you find it in the work itself — and the one thing that most often goes wrong when people quote Yangming.

[Quote source](https://www.philosophydef.com/quote-source) / Wang Yangming

How to cite this author, and what circulates under the name that is not theirs to give.

### Sourcing profile

Language of the works

Classical Chinese

Cited here from

Instructions for Practical Living (Chuanxilu), by juan and entry, plus one entry recorded as traditional last words.

How to cite it

Juan (volume) and entry number. The Chuanxilu is a record of conversations and letters compiled by disciples, and the numbering is what identifies an entry.

Where quotations of this author go wrong

The famous deathbed saying attributed to him is not in the Chuanxilu; it is a traditional attribution recorded by later followers, and this archive files it as such. Wang also used 知行合一 (“the unity of knowledge and action”) as a technical term against Zhu Xi's teaching, so the phrase does not mean what “knowledge and action go together” suggests to a modern reader.

### Frequently asked questions

#### Where can I check quotations attributed to Wang Yangming?

Juan (volume) and entry number. The Chuanxilu is a record of conversations and letters compiled by disciples, and the numbering is what identifies an entry. This archive cites Wang Yangming from Instructions for Practical Living (Chuanxilu), by juan and entry, plus one entry recorded as traditional last words. Every passage listed on this page carries that locator, so it can be found in any edition of the work.

#### What is the most common mistake when quoting Wang Yangming?

The famous deathbed saying attributed to him is not in the Chuanxilu; it is a traditional attribution recorded by later followers, and this archive files it as such. Wang also used 知行合一 (“the unity of knowledge and action”) as a technical term against Zhu Xi's teaching, so the phrase does not mean what “knowledge and action go together” suggests to a modern reader.

#### What language did Wang Yangming write in?

Classical Chinese. Any English sentence you read is a translation, so a complete source names the translator as well as the passage.
